title: Steak bites with corn salsa and guacamole

items: 1 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 Tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)
1½ cups corn kernels (frozen and thawed, or canned and drained)
1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained

steps: Make the salsa. In a medium bowl, toss the corn, beans, red pepper, onion, cilantro, 2 Tbsp lime juice and ½ tsp salt.
Make the guacamole. Halve and pit the avocados and scoop them into a second bowl. Mash with a fork, leaving it a little chunky. Stir in 1 Tbsp lime juice and ½ tsp salt.
Pat the steak cubes dry with paper towels. Dry meat browns and wet meat steams. Toss with the chili powder, ¾ tsp salt and the pepper.

Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke, about 3 min. Add the oil, then the steak in a single layer with space between pieces. Work in 2 batches if they don't fit.
Sear 1–2 min without moving, until a dark crust forms. Turn with tongs and cook 1–2 min more. Pull at 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140–145°F for medium. Rest 3 min.
Spoon the salsa onto plates, pile the steak bites on top and add a scoop of guacamole in the middle.
tips: Don't crowd the pan. Too many pieces at once drop the heat and the steak turns gray instead of brown.
Make the salsa up to 1 day ahead. Make the guacamole last so it stays green.
Swap the steak for shrimp. Sear 1–2 min per side, until pink and opaque.
storage: Steak and salsa keep in the fridge up to 3 days in separate containers. Reheat the steak in a hot skillet 1–2 min so it doesn't overcook. Guacamole browns within a day, so make only what you'll eat.
